units.title: Implement host installation audit and safe config planning
units.objective: Produce strict read-only installation receipts and idempotent dry-run plans for Codex and Claude host hooks without changing live configuration.

included: Strict Pydantic installation receipt and hook-surface contracts
Read-only audit of host and repository hook presence, digest, and duplicate risk
Atomic-backup-aware but dry-run-only host config merge planning
Both-sign JSON, TOML, missing, drifted, and unrelated-hook fixtures
excluded: Live client restart, trust, message send, or acknowledgement

outputs: Read-only audit CLI with stable JSON output
Dry-run host config merge plan that preserves unrelated hooks

acceptance.criterion: Fixture audits distinguish absent, drifted, configured, unknown-trust, and operationally-observed states without writing files or promoting configuration to runtime proof.
evidence_required: pytest -q tests/test_mailbox_delivery.py -k 'installation or config or audit'
ruff and strict mypy on the new contracts and CLIs
acceptance.negative_control: Malformed JSON/TOML, unrelated hooks, missing adapters, and configured-without-receipt fixtures must retain exact content or fail before producing a repairable state.

units.title: Make Codex and Claude lifecycle adapters duplicate-safe
units.objective: Allow host and repository compatibility hooks to coexist during migration while emitting one agent-visible notice per message and lifecycle event.

included: Client-specific event normalization into one delivery-event identity
Codex and Claude adapter parity
Duplicate suppression without acknowledgement inference
Repository-local compatibility behavior and both-sign tests
excluded: Mailbox routing or acknowledgement schema replacement

outputs: Duplicate-safe Codex and Claude lifecycle adapters

dependencies.rationale: Adapter behavior must emit the installation and runtime states frozen by MF-01.

acceptance.criterion: For each client, two matching host/repository hook invocations for one lifecycle event produce one visible notice and one observation receipt, while a later lifecycle event repeats an unacknowledged request.
evidence_required: pytest -q tests/test_coordination_messages.py tests/test_mailbox_delivery.py -k 'hook or duplicate or lifecycle'
ruff and strict mypy on changed runtime surfaces
acceptance.negative_control: Wrong session, unknown claim, acknowledged message, expired message, unsupported event, and missing event identity must not create a false observation or acknowledgement.

units.title: Install and activate workstation-level Codex and Claude hooks
units.objective: Safely install the accepted adapters in Brian's user-level Codex and Claude lifecycle configuration and prove idempotent configuration readback.

included: Timestamped backups of exact user hook configuration files
Atomic merge of only canonical mailbox hook blocks
Post-write parse/readback and idempotent second dry run
Operator hook trust review and client restart/resume checklist
excluded: Deletion of unrelated or repository-local hooks
Claims of live delivery before receipts exist

outputs: Backed-up and atomically updated Codex and Claude user hook configurations
Idempotent dry-run result and explicit trust/restart state

dependencies.rationale: Host and repository hooks may coexist only after duplicate-safe adapters are accepted.

acceptance.criterion: Both user configurations parse, retain unrelated hooks, contain one canonical mailbox hook per required event, produce exact backup paths, and yield no actions on a second dry run.
evidence_required: Second dry run with zero actions
Codex /hooks review plus Codex and Claude restart/resume state recorded
acceptance.negative_control: A malformed config, failed backup, changed candidate between review and write, or untrusted hook aborts promotion to operational state.

failed_guards: Exact host-config candidate has not received readiness approval

units.title: Audit the registered governed-repository fleet
units.objective: Produce one read-only fleet report that classifies mailbox compatibility drift and emits exact separately claimable repair packets without changing consumer repositories.

included: governed_repos.yaml as the explicit fleet inventory
Read-only installation receipt for every registered repository
Current, drifted, unavailable, and excluded classifications
One exact bounded repair command and path list per drifted repository
excluded: Consumer repository mutation, claims, commits, pushes, or merges
Adding repositories to the registry without authority review
Treating repository hooks as proof of host operation

outputs: Explicit inventory omissions including DIGIMON if still absent

dependencies.rationale: Fleet classification reuses the accepted installation receipt contract.

acceptance.criterion: One command audits every explicit fleet entry without writes, reports omissions separately, and produces a concrete repair packet for each drifted repository.
evidence_required: Fixture fleet with current, drifted, missing, and excluded repositories
git status proving no consumer repository changed
acceptance.negative_control: Dirty, archived, employer-owned, absent, unregistered, or authority-unknown repositories are reported and never repaired automatically.

units.title: Certify all Codex and Claude delivery directions
units.objective: Produce one exact four-leg certification showing persisted, observed, and acknowledged evidence for every Codex/Claude sender-recipient pairing.

included: Codex-to-Codex, Claude-to-Claude, Codex-to-Claude, and Claude-to-Codex legs
Exact live claimed sessions and lifecycle events
Four distinct message IDs and exact observation/acknowledgement receipt IDs
Configured-without-observation and acknowledged-hidden negative controls
excluded: Asynchronous interruption or latency SLO claims
Inference that the requested work was completed

outputs: Human-readable status summary linked to exact receipts
Negative-control proof that configuration alone is not operation

dependencies.rationale: Live certification requires installed and activated host hooks.
Fleet configuration evidence bounds which repository contexts the certification represents.

conflict_surfaces.target: Canonical cross-client mailbox and four active runtime sessions

acceptance.criterion: All four exact sender-recipient directions reach acknowledged state through real lifecycle delivery and validate as one MailboxDeliveryCertificationV1.
evidence_required: Certification schema validation and source revision
acceptance.negative_control: A persisted-only, manually polled-as-recipient, wrong-session, expired, duplicate-injected, or configuration-only leg fails certification.

failed_guards: Four exact active recipient sessions are not yet bound
